chunks: From him, from Fadala, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'If the one in Ihram plays with his beard and a hair (or eight hairs) fall from it,' he said, 'He feeds (a poor person) something.'

key_terms.المُحْرِمُ: The one in Ihram (ritual state for Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.شَيْئًا: Something (referring to a measure of food)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty if a person in Ihram plucks hairs from their beard?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfahar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that accidentally plucking beard hairs while playing with them incurs a fidyah of feeding a poor person, distinguishing it from more severe penalties for deliberate acts. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of differentiating between minor, unintentional breaches of Ihram restrictions and major violations, emphasizing ease for the pilgrim. The specific mention of the beard underscores its significance as a protected area during the state of consecration.
